title: Buyer Objection Matrix for Platform Sellers (rough)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, field-ready matrix that helps platform sellers (SEs, AEs, CS leads) triage buyer objections and pick a compact play: 30–90s scripts, technical backup points, and escalation rules. Rough draft for rapid testing with 10 pilot conversations.

Audience:
- Platform sellers working mid-market to enterprise
- Solutions engineers during discovery and procurement calls

One-liner to use with buyers:
"Redwood gives you predictable inference economics with production controls — we help you pick a deployment mode that keeps apps online, low-latency, and cost-managed."

How to use this doc (field steps):
1) Identify the objection bucket. 2) Use the 30s script in the right-hand column. 3) If buyer asks for technical depth, drop into the technical backup bullet. 4) If risk/regulatory objection, follow escalation.

Objection buckets + plays (compact):
- "Cost too high / vendor expensive":
  - 30s script: "We understand — most teams we talk to start with our hosted API to validate ROI, then move to Dedicated or Private when they need predictable unit economics. We can run a simple cost-to-value sim in 48 hours."
  - Technical backup: show batching/kv-cache examples, quantization choices and sample cost delta (-30% tokens with prefix caching).
  - Escalation: offer a pilot estimate (2-week) + commit to per-token baseline.

- "Latency/SLO concerns / can't rely on third-party":
  - 30s script: "Redwood's routing and dedicated capacity options let you pin latency SLOs and fail over to regional capacity automatically. We also support private deployments for full network control."
  - Technical backup: routing policy graphic (talk through canary + fallback), Recent SLA numbers (p99 tail), tracing hooks in Console.
  - Escalation: propose a dedicated capacity POC with synthetic traffic and SLO verification.

- "Security / data residency / compliance":
  - 30s script: "We support Private (VPC and on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations and full audit logs — show me the baseline compliance needs and we can map controls in next meeting."
  - Technical backup: KMS providers list, audit-log schema, encryption-at-rest details, SOC2/ISO pointers.
  - Escalation: 引 offer security review workshop with Security & Compliance SME.

- "Model quality / hallucinations / output regression":
  - 30s script: "We provide model evals and prompt-run baselines; when quality matters we can anchor on curated model variants plus reranking and safety policies."
  - Technical backup: eval harness sample, rollback + canary strategy, Optimize toolkit for quality monitoring.
  - Escalation: run a small labeled eval with customer prompts (7–10 test cases).

- "We want to self-host / avoid vendor lock-in":
  - 30s script: "We get it — Redwood runs everywhere: hosted to private to on-prem. The same API and rollout controls let you migrate without rewriting code."
  - Technical backup: sample migration checklist, version pinning, model compat table.
  - Escalation: propose a hybrid pilot: hosted for speed, private for regulated flows.

Quick rebut templates (30–60s):
- "Your price sounds higher than X": "Totally — can I walk you through what’s included? For example, we bake in autoscaling, KV cache, and tracing — those reduce ops and token spend downstream. If you want, I'll run a side-by-side cost model with your workload."
- "We can't risk downtime": "We design for graceful degradation: automatic fallbacks to lower-tier models and regional failover with tracing to help root-cause. We can run a simulated outage drill in the POC."

Suggested slide sequence for a 10-slide deck (pilot-ready):
1) Title + one-line value prop
2) Deployment options + decision checklist
3) Performance + economics quickbench (sample numbers)
4) Objection matrix summary (this doc condensed)
5) Routing & fallback architecture (diagram)
6) Security controls + compliance map
7) Quality & eval gating (before/after examples)
8) Pilot plan + success metrics
9) Commercial outline + options
10) Next steps / contacts

Open questions / things to validate in pilots:
- Typical sequence length distribution from buyer workloads (affects batching/kv economics)
- Acceptable latency p99 targets and burst traffic windows
- Existing KMS / IAM constraints and audit retention needs

Next steps (owner: Aisha):
- Fold feedback from SE pilot (10 calls) — due 2025-10-09
- Create a one-page cheat-sheet for AEs with 8 scripts (format: Slack snippet)
- Sync with Security SME for a standard compliance play doc

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a microsite generator: input buyer tags → produce a 4-slide deck + seller script
- Add a tiny simulator for cost/latency tradeoffs sellers can run live in demo
- Keep language punchy; buyer scripts must be <60s spoken.
